content.comment_body: Hello, I have a new [product_name] [article_no], and my issue is that after loading a program, everything works while running and connected. However, if I disconnect and reconnect the power, the program disappears. Have I overlooked something?
The program in the [product_name] is stored on Flash EPROM, so power loss shouldn't erase it. Are you sure it's a [article_no]? Not a different [article_no] version?
I mistyped, it is a [article_no]. I also suspect the flash memory may be faulty.
I've never encountered a case where flash memory fails in the [product_name]. What exactly happens once the power returns?
It starts up and shows 'No Program Press ESC'. The clock keeps the correct date and time, but the program is gone. I tried programming both via keypad and PC, same result. The module is [article_no].
That's odd. It really does seem like a flash memory failure. You may want to contact support.

Hello [user_name], unfortunately, I have experienced this too and had to replace mine. My [product_name] also experienced frequent power cycles due to a connection mistake, where the power was cut instead of an input. Maybe that's related. Mine was a [article_no] as well.

Hi, I've worked with [product_name] for years and haven't seen this issue before. Possible reasons for losing a program in [product_name] [version_no]: + If a memory card is used and copy protection is enabled, unplugging the card deletes the program because copy protection requires that specific card to be present. Try disabling copy protection. + An operator manually deleted the program. In early [version_no], if a password-protected program receives three incorrect attempts, it is automatically deleted; this was changed in later versions. Consider securing access to the cabinet. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Several users share their experiences regarding program loss after power cycling a [product_name] [article_no]. The issue is unexpected since the device is supposed to retain programs via Flash EPROM. Users express concern, having tried different upload methods and confirmed hardware is handled properly, yet confusion persists about the root cause.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] [article_no] to reliably keep programs in non-volatile memory, so that interruptions in power do not result in program loss, as described in the product documentation.
